problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=\frac{4}{(t+1)^{3}}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=1$ and velocity $v=-\frac{1}{2}$ when $t=1$, calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$

feedback.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration 

$$
a(t)=\frac{8}{(t+2)^{3}},
$$

where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=0$ and velocity $v=1$ when $t=0,$ the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$x(t)=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{8}{(t+2)^{3}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =8\int (t+2)^{-3}\,\text{d}t \\  & =8\cdot \frac{(t+2)^{-2}}{-2}+C \\  & =-\frac{4}{(t+2)^{2}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-\frac{4}{(0+2)^{2}}+C \\ 1 & =-\frac{4}{4}+C \\ 1 & =-1+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by 

$$
v(t)=-\frac{4}{(t+2)^{2}}+2.
$$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-\frac{4}{(t+2)^{2}}+2)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-4\int (t+2)^{-2}\,\text{d}t+2\int \,\text{d}t \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{(t+2)^{-1}}{-1}+2t+K \\  & =\frac{4}{t+2}+2t+K.\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =\frac{4}{0+2}+0+K \\ 0 & =2+K \\ K & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{4}{t+2}+2t-2.
$$
